provenance_summary: V1-B first expansion wave. Graphene oxide (GO) and reduced GO adsorbents with large SSA and abundant functional groups (-COOH, -OH, C-O-C) for heavy metal and dye removal.

mechanisms.description: Electrostatic attraction: negatively charged GO surface (-COO⁻, -O⁻) attracts cationic pollutants at pH > pHpzc

pollutant_feature.text: Cationic dyes and heavy metal ions

bio_structure.text: Carboxyl (-COOH), hydroxyl (-OH), epoxy (C-O-C) groups on GO

interaction.text: Electrostatic attraction to deprotonated oxygen groups

why_it_works.text: High adsorption capacity for cationic dyes and heavy metals

engineering_constraints.description: GO synthesis: modified Hummers method (KMnO₄, NaNO₃, H₂SO₄ oxidation of graphite)

design_translation.idea: Use graphene oxide with abundant oxygen groups as base material for heavy metal and dye adsorption; combine with polymers, magnetic particles, or other materials for enhanced performance and recyclability
examples: Magnetic GO composites for recyclable dye removal
design_translation.applicability: Heavy metal and dye removal from wastewater; composite base material for enhanced adsorbents

knowledge_gaps: Pure GO adsorption capacity is relatively low; composites needed for practical applications
Cost of GO production at industrial scale
Restacking behavior in real wastewater conditions

narrative.text: Graphene oxide is a 2D carbon nanomaterial with large specific surface area and abundant oxygen-containing groups. Its unique structure enables both physical (π-π, van der Waals) and chemical (electrostatic, coordination) adsorption mechanisms.
